title: Rep. Cleo Fields Disclosed 3 Purchases: Netflix, Microsoft and Apple (Oct 1)
content:
Rep. Cleo Fields (LA-06) disclosed three stock purchases on October 1, 2026, dated between September 8 and September 14: Netflix (NFLX), Microsoft (MSFT) and Apple (AAPL).

Trade data: Bargo, compiled from U.S. House and Senate STOCK Act filings.

TickerCompanyTransaction dateType / sizePrice at purchase vs. Oct 2 (Bargo est.)
NFLXNetflix, Inc.Sep 14, 2026Purchase, $1,001–$15,000$80.32 vs. $67.06 (−16.51%)
MSFTMicrosoft CorporationSep 10, 2026Purchase, $1,001–$15,000$492.44 vs. $517.53 (+5.10%)
AAPLApple Inc.Sep 8, 2026Purchase, $1,001–$15,000$316.22 vs. $333.69 (+5.52%)

Disclosure date for all three: Oct 1, 2026 (17 to 23 days after the trades). Member: Rep. Cleo Fields, LA-06 (House).

What's been disclosed

  • Three purchases: Netflix ($1,001–$15,000) on September 14, Microsoft ($1,001–$15,000) on September 10 and Apple ($1,001–$15,000) on September 8.
  • Price since: Bargo's estimate puts Netflix about 16.5% lower on October 2 than on the purchase date, Microsoft about 5.1% higher and Apple about 5.5% higher.
  • Row count: Bargo's data lists 4 rows for this filing. The Microsoft row appears twice with identical details, which leaves the 3 distinct trades shown above.

Quick FAQ

Why does the post say 3 trades when the data has 4 rows?
Two Microsoft rows are exact copies. The data does not show whether they are a duplicate entry or two separate transactions with identical details, so we count the 3 distinct trades.

How long after the purchases were they disclosed?
17 to 23 days. The STOCK Act gives members 45 days from the transaction to disclose it.

Why are the amounts ranges?
Filings report value bands such as $1,001–$15,000 instead of exact dollar amounts.

Where does the price comparison come from?
It is Bargo's estimate, comparing the price on the transaction date with the October 2 price. It is not the member's actual execution price.

Trade data from Bargo (STOCK Act filings). This post is our own summary of public filings and is not investment advice. See our Disclaimer and evidence labels.
